_comment: Tune per project. This file may set 'severity', 'ignore' and 'staleness' ONLY: a 'patterns' key is refused (exit 2), as is an all-'warn' severity map, an unrecognised severity value, and a catch-all ignore. An ignore pattern blanks the region of text it matches before detection runs, and also drops any finding whose span it fullmatches; keep each one as narrow as the false positive requires ('\b4471\b', never '\d+'), because a broad ignore CAN silence a whole category. Every ignore pattern in effect is printed on every run — that visibility is the only check on how wide you make them. The shipped entry exempts genuine DATE FORMATS (ISO and written) only. A bare year is a claim and is flagged. The 'retracted' category is NOT listed under severity and cannot be tuned: a Changed or Contradicted entry is this register's own statement that the wording is no longer sayable, so downgrading it would be a per-claim waiver, and there is no per-claim waiver.
_staleness: max_age_days is how long a ' — checked:' date stays good before a claim leaning on it is reported. severity is error or warn. require_checked makes an undated Cleared entry report too — leave it false until the register is actually dated, then turn it on. All three print on every run: a long max_age_days is a weakening and has to be visible in the same output as the verdict it produced.
